Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Gov’t pursuing expenditure-based consolidation to curb reckless spending – Ricketts-Hagan Source : Emma Ankrah 18 November 2026 5:51pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Deputy Majority Leader and Member of Parliament for Cape Coast, George Kweku Ricketts-Hagan, says the government is pursuing an expenditure-based fiscal consolidation approach to align public spending with available revenue and reduce excessive borrowing.
Contributing to the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Wednesday, novemer 18, he said the strategy marks a departure from what he described as the previous administration's reliance on borrowing to finance government expenditure.
Mr Ricketts-Hagan argued that the current government's fiscal approach was helping to restore discipline in public spending and improve the economy.
He accused the previous administration of prioritising revenue mobilisation to support expenditure rather than controlling spending to match available resources.
“Instead of doing an expenditure-based consolidation, they were doing a revenue-based one. They were more interested in borrowing money to fund expenditure,” he said.
Mr Ricketts-Hagan said the current administration was instead ensuring that government expenditure corresponded with the revenue available.
“We are doing an expenditure-based consolidation, which means that we are cutting our coat according to our size. We are matching our expenditure to our revenue,” he told Parliament.
He added that the government was avoiding what he described as reckless and frivolous spending, while directing available resources to priority sectors of the economy.
Mr Ricketts-Hagan attributed the improvement in key economic indicators to the government's fiscal discipline and spending controls.
He said the measures had contributed to the economic recovery recorded under President John Dramani Mahama's administration.
